reading.text:
UNIT def:LevyStochCalc.Probability.ProgressivelyMeasurable
Standing setting (paper section 2, intro (eq:mvfbsdej), section 3 solution space, section 4,
appendix A): (Omega, F, (F_t), P) satisfying the usual conditions, horizon T > 0; a d-dim
Brownian motion W and an independent Poisson random measure N on R_+ x E with intensity
dt nu(de), nu sigma-finite on a countably generated (E, calE); (F_t) is the usual augmentation
of the filtration generated by W, N and an independent initial sigma-field F_0. The compensated
measure is Ntilde(dt,de) = N(dt,de) - dt nu(de). Integrands U of the Poisson integral are
predictable: P (x) calE-measurable, P the predictable sigma-field on Omega x [0,T]
(eq:fubiniiso), with E int_0^T ||U_t||^2_{L2(nu)} dt < infinity (the space H^2_N). The
integral int_0^t int_E U_s(e) Ntilde(ds,de) is the standard L2 (Ito-Levy) compensated-Poisson
integral: an L2 martingale, cadlag, with the isometry E|int_0^t int U dNtilde|^2 =
E int_0^t ||U_s||^2 ds (used in Lemma 4.1 "true L2-martingales by the Ito and
compensated-Poisson isometries"), jumps Delta = U_s(e) at atoms (s,e) of N, and for integrands
in L1(dP dt nu) the integral splits as int U dN - int U nu ds (eq:compid, eq:zeromean).
Progressive measurability is used for the coefficient processes b, sigma, f and the forcings
q^b, q^sigma, q^f (eq:coefmeas, section 4); predictability (P (x) calE) for h and q^h.

Reading.
Paper notion: progressive measurability ((eq:coefmeas): the coefficient processes b, sigma, f
along a diagonal input; forcings q^b, q^sigma, q^f in section 4) with respect to (F_t): for each
t, the restriction of (s, omega) -> X(s, omega) to [0,t] x Omega is B([0,t]) (x) F_t-measurable.
Faithful Lean: for every t, Measurable[ (Borel on [0,t] or {s <= t}) (x) F_t ] of the restriction
(Mathlib's ProgMeasurable, or an equivalent formulation on the full time type with the subtype
{s // s <= t}). Equivalence with Mathlib's ProgMeasurable would be the cleanest; any formulation
equivalent to it is faithful.

comparison.text:
Lean (LevyStochCalc/Probability/Progressive.lean): ProgressivelyMeasurable F H := for every t in R,
(omega, s) -> indicator_{Iic t}(H omega) s is strongly measurable for F t (x) Borel(R) on
Omega x R. Proved equivalent to Mathlib's IsStronglyProgressive (isStronglyProgressive,
of_isStronglyProgressive).
Comparison with the locked reading: progressive measurability (restriction to times <= t is
B (x) F_t-measurable), stated through the indicator truncation instead of the subtype
[0,t]; equivalence with Mathlib's notion proved, which the reading named as the cleanest
criterion. Strong measurability equals measurability for the paper's finite-dimensional targets.
Representation choices: time axis R (negative times included); truncation by an indicator (value
0 after t) instead of restriction - equivalent (proved). Harmless.

verdict.detail:
Representation choices: (1) truncation by the indicator of (-inf,t] (value 0 after t) on the full
Omega x R instead of restriction to [0,t] x Omega - proved equivalent to Mathlib's
IsStronglyProgressive; (2) time axis R (negative times included); (3) strong measurability,
equivalent to measurability for finite-dimensional targets.
